skill.name: dependency-upgrade
skill.description: Plan major dependency upgrades with semver review, compatibility checks, staged updates, tests, automation examples, and rollback guidance.
skill.summary: Guides staged dependency upgrades with compatibility checks, testing, automation, and rollback planning.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, not actual Ruby or shell backtick execution. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden malicious instructions. The skill includes legitimate high-impact package, network, and filesystem examples, so users should review commands and diffs before execution.

remediation.issue: Unpinned or high-impact commands can change dependency state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, prefer dry runs, pin npx tools, and document rollback before running package manager or git commands.

remediation.issue: Migration script examples write source files in bulk.
remediation.suggestion: Add backup, dry-run, diff review, and path allowlist guidance before fs.writeFileSync examples.

remediation.issue: The changelog example fetches remote content with curl.
remediation.suggestion: Advise users to inspect official changelog pages or fetched content before acting on remote documentation.

remediation.issue: Force and legacy peer dependency examples can mask conflicts.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend these flags only as a last resort with notes for follow-up peer dependency remediation.

content.value_statement: Major dependency upgrades can break builds, tests, and runtime behavior. This skill structures the work into analysis, staged updates, validation, automation, and rollback.
actual_capabilities: Explains semantic version ranges and what major, minor, and patch changes imply.
Lists npm and yarn commands for outdated packages, audits, duplicates, and dependency trees.
Outlines staged upgrade phases for planning, incremental updates, validation, and rollback.
Shows React compatibility, testing, codemod, Renovate, and Dependabot examples.
Provides a practical pre-upgrade, during-upgrade, and post-upgrade checklist.
limitations: It does not inspect a repository by itself or produce live dependency results.
Examples focus on JavaScript, npm, yarn, and React workflows.
Commands and codemods can change files and should require user approval.
Referenced resource files are named in SKILL.md but are not present in this package.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Frontend Framework
use_cases.description: Plan a React or routing upgrade with compatibility checks, staged package changes, tests, and rollback notes.

use_cases.title: Patch Vulnerable Dependencies
use_cases.description: Turn audit findings into a prioritized update plan with validation steps and peer dependency review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Update Automation
use_cases.description: Prepare Renovate or Dependabot policies that separate routine updates from major version review.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Upgrade Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my dependency list. Identify outdated major versions, risky packages, and a staged first plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Framework Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan an upgrade from my current framework version to the target version. Include compatibility risks and test gates.

prompt_templates.title: Design Validation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create validation coverage for a dependency upgrade. Include unit, integration, visual, build, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Automated Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a dependency automation policy. Separate patch, minor, and major updates, and define review rules.

output_examples.input: Upgrade React 17 to React 18 in a TypeScript app.
output: A staged upgrade order with React, React DOM, routing, testing libraries, and build tooling.
A compatibility checklist for peer dependencies and changed APIs.
A validation plan covering build, tests, visual checks, and rollback.

output_examples.input: A dependency audit found a vulnerable package that needs a major update.
output: A risk summary for the vulnerable package and dependent libraries.
A plan to update one major version at a time with test checkpoints.
A review list for changelog notes, peer warnings, and lock file changes.

output_examples.input: Set up automated dependency update rules for a team repository.
output: A policy that automates low-risk updates and routes major changes for review.
Suggested labels, schedules, reviewer expectations, and merge conditions.
A warning list for peer dependency conflicts and failing test gates.

best_practices: Create a branch and capture a passing test baseline before any upgrade.
Upgrade one major dependency at a time and review changelogs before each step.
Run unit, integration, build, and regression checks after each meaningful change.
anti_patterns: Upgrading every package in one pass without a rollback plan.
Using force install flags to bypass peer dependency warnings without analysis.
Running codemods or migration scripts without reviewing the diff.

faq.question: Does this skill run upgrades automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and example commands that need user approval.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does it cover best?
faq.answer: It mainly covers JavaScript, npm, yarn, React, testing libraries, Renovate, and Dependabot.

faq.question: Can it replace changelog review?
faq.answer: No. It encourages changelog and migration guide review before version changes.

faq.question: Does it include working scripts?
faq.answer: The reviewed package contains SKILL.md examples only; referenced resources are not present in the file tree.

faq.question: How should I handle major versions?
faq.answer: Upgrade one major version at a time, run tests, and document fixes before continuing.

faq.question: Is it useful for security updates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help plan vulnerable dependency updates, but security fixes still need validation.
